Flight Club Challenge: Cool Down Combo 🦉

🚀 Flight Club Challenge

Wrap up your kicking & striking unit with a chill-out combo. Three stretches to keep your body bendy and happy. 🌈

1
Flamingo Stretch (Quadriceps)

How to do it:

  • Stand tall and bend one knee, bringing your foot behind you.
  • Hold your ankle with your hand and keep your balance.
  • Keep your knees close together and hold for 10 seconds.
  • Switch legs and repeat.
  • Optional: Extend one arm forward like a flamingo's neck! 🦩

Benefits: Stretches the front of the thigh (quadriceps) and improves balance.

2
Forearm Plank

How to do it:

  • Get into a plank position with forearms on the ground and back flat.
  • Hold for 30 seconds without dropping your belly.
  • Challenge: Try tapping one shoulder at a time while holding the plank.
  • Modification: Try a knee plank if needed.

Benefits: Builds core and upper body strength.

3
Toe Touch Stretch (Waterfall)

How to do it:

  • Stand up tall with feet together.
  • Slowly bend forward and reach for your toes, keeping legs straight.
  • Let your arms flow down like a waterfall. 💧
  • Hold for 10 seconds, then slowly stand up.

Benefits: Stretches hamstrings and lower back.

🏃Activity Cue

Submit a video or a guardian's note saying you completed it!

✅Flight Crew Check-In

Flight Crew, check in!

  • Which stretch helped you cool down the most?
  • How does your body feel now compared to before?

Unit 1.10

Flight Club: Card Challenge 🃏

🚀 Flight Club Challenge

Game time! Use a deck of cards to power your workout. Every card = a different exercise. Are you ready, card sharks? 🎴

1
Setup
Materials You Need
  • 🎴 Option 1: A real deck of playing cards
  • 💻 Option 2: Internet access + the Calculator Soup Random Card Generator
2
How to Play
Step by Step
1
Draw a Card

Real deck: shuffle and draw one card at a time.

Online: click DRAW to see your card.

2
Match the Card to the Exercise

The SUIT tells you the exercise. The NUMBER tells you how many reps.

  • ♥️ Hearts = Jumping Jacks (8♥ = 8 jumping jacks)
  • ♠️ Spades = Push-Ups (K♠ = 13 push-ups)
  • ♦️ Diamonds = Sit-Ups / Crunches (4♦ = 4 sit-ups)
  • ♣️ Clubs = Squats (J♣ = 11 squats)

Face card values: Ace = 14, King = 13, Queen = 12, Jack = 11. Number cards = their number.

3
Pick Your Level
  • 🌱 Beginner — Draw 10 cards
  • ⭐ Intermediate — Draw 15 cards
  • 🚀 Advanced — Draw 20 cards

Complete the exercise BEFORE drawing another card!

🏃Activity Cue

Submit a video OR a guardian's statement saying you completed it!

✅Flight Crew Check-In

Flight Crew, check in!

  • Which suit did you draw the most?
  • Which exercise turned out to be your favorite?

Unit 1.11

Flight Club: Dice Challenge 🎲

🚀 Flight Club Challenge

Roll the dice, take your chances! Every number gets a different exercise. How will your workout go? Only fate knows! 🎲

1
Setup
Materials You Need
  • 🎲 One die (real or virtual)
  • 💻 Online option: Calculator Soup Dice Roller
  • 📏 Comfortable space to move
  • ⏱️ Timer or clock
2
How to Play
Step by Step
1
Roll the Die

Roll once. Look at your number.

2
Match Number to Exercise
  • 🎲 1 = Jumping Jacks — 10 reps
  • 🎲 2 = Push-Ups — 5 reps
  • 🎲 3 = Squats — 5 reps
  • 🎲 4 = Sit-Ups or Crunches — 10 reps
  • 🎲 5 = High Knees — 10 seconds
  • 🎲 6 = Mountain Climbers — 10 reps
3
Complete the Exercise

Do the exercise, then roll AGAIN for your next movement.

4
Repeat 10–12 Times

That's about a 10-minute full workout. 🔥

🏃Activity Cue

Optional Challenge Rounds:

  • 🆙 Level Up — Add 5 reps each round, or do all 6 exercises ONCE for a "Full Dice Circuit"
  • 👯 Partner Mode — Take turns rolling; each person does what the other rolls
  • ❤️ Cardio Boost — Add a 30-second jog in place between rolls
💭Think About It

Reflect:

  • Which exercise challenged you the most, and why?
  • How did your energy level change as you went?
  • How does this type of activity support YOUR fitness goals?
✅Flight Crew Check-In

Flight Crew, check in!

  • What number came up the most?
  • Did you push past your comfort zone?

Touch every wall, fly through the cycles, master your balance and personal space. Let's GO! 🏃

Move SAFELY to touch 3 or 4 different walls while practicing balance, coordination, and safe movement.

assignments.title: Water Rescue Heroes 🛟
assignments.html:
Optima
Academy Online
Mission: Move!
3rd Grade PE · Unit 1.17 · Water Safety & Swim Skills
Week 33

Water Rescue Heroes 🛟

You learned the golden rule — Reach or Throw, Don't Go! Now show what you know. Choose ONE option below and prove you'd know exactly what to do in a water emergency.

1
Option 1
🎨 Rescue Helper Poster

Draw a poster showing THREE different items that could help someone in a water emergency.

  • Label each item with its NAME
  • Write REACH or THROW next to each one
  • Add one sentence: "You should never jump in because…"
2
Option 2
🎬 Rescue Reporter Video

Do the scavenger hunt for real! Find two things in your home that could help in a water emergency (one to REACH with, one to THROW). Record a short video where you:

  • Show each item and say whether it's for reaching or throwing
  • Explain WHY each one would work
  • Say the golden rule out loud: "Reach or throw, don't go!"
3
Option 3
✍️ Write the Plan

Imagine you're at a pool and a friend starts struggling in the water. Write 3–5 complete sentences answering:

  • What is the FIRST thing you do? (Hint: it uses your voice! 📣)
  • What TWO items nearby could you use to help, and how?
  • Why should you NEVER jump in after them?
🏃Activity Cue

Safety first: This is a THINKING assignment — practice your reach and throw moves on dry land only! Never practice rescues in real water. 🦺

✅Check for Understanding

Before you submit, make sure your work shows: at least 2 rescue helper items, whether each is for reaching or throwing, and the reason you stay on land. That's a perfect score waiting to happen! 🌟

→What's Next

Up next: the Swim Skills Check — grab a guardian, it's their turn to help!

assignments.title: Swim Skills Check 🏊 (Guardian Helper Needed!)
assignments.html:
Optima
Academy Online
Mission: Move!
3rd Grade PE · Unit 1.17 · Water Safety & Swim Skills
Week 34

Swim Skills Check 🏊 (Guardian Helper Needed!)

Florida 3rd graders learn to put basic swim skills together (standard PE.3.M.1.6). This one is a TEAM assignment — you bring the swim skills, your guardian brings the eyeballs and the paperwork. Pick the option that fits your family!

🦺Guardians, Read First

Water portions of this assignment are 100% optional and must happen ONLY with your direct, in-the-water-area supervision, in water your child is comfortable in. No pool? No problem — Option B needs zero water. If your child is not yet a swimmer, we strongly encourage swim lessons through your local YMCA, county aquatic center, or Red Cross provider — and Option B works great in the meantime.

1
Option A
💧 In-the-Water Skills Check

With a guardian watching, show as many of these basic swim skills as you can — then put two or more together in a row (that's the "combination" part!):

🪜
Safe Entry & Exit
Get in and out of the water safely (steps, ladder, or seated slide-in).
🫧
Bubbles & Breath Control
Put your face in the water and blow bubbles for 3 seconds.
🌊
Front Float
Float on your front for 5 seconds (guardian or wall nearby).
⭐
Back Float
Float on your back for 5 seconds — ears in, belly up!
🦵
Flutter Kick
Hold the wall or a kickboard and kick small, fast kicks.
💪
Arm Strokes
Big scooping arm circles — try kicks + arms together for a few yards.

Example combinations: safe entry → bubbles → front float, or kickboard kicks → back float → safe exit. Two or more skills in a row = mission complete! 🎉

2
Option B
🏠 Dry-Land Swim Skills (No Pool Needed)

No safe water access right now? Show your swim-skill KNOWLEDGE on dry land:

  • 🛏️ Lie on a bed or soft floor and demonstrate the front float position (arms out, body straight) and flutter kick
  • 💪 Stand up and show arm stroke circles while marching your flutter kick — "air swimming!"
  • 🗣️ Tell your guardian (or the camera) the steps of a combination you would do in a pool: "First I would enter safely, then blow bubbles, then front float…"
  • 🦺 Bonus: say one water safety rule from this unit
3
Step 3
📋 Guardian Documentation (Required)

Guardians: submit ONE of the following with your student's work — a short video clip, photos, or simply copy, complete, and submit this statement as a text entry or comment:

"I confirm that my student, ______________________, completed the Swim Skills Check on (date) __________ under my direct supervision.

They completed (circle/keep one): Option A — in the water / Option B — dry land.

Skills demonstrated (list them): ______________________________________________.

Guardian name & signature: ______________________"

💡Did You Know?

Floating is the #1 survival skill in the water — even before swimming fast! If you ever get tired in the water, flip onto your back, float like a starfish, and call for help. Rest floats save lives. ⭐

→What's Next

That wraps the Water Safety unit — you're officially a Water Rescue Hero AND a smarter swimmer. Next stop: your end-of-year Fitness Check-In, Round 2!
